text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- Families with several children to be adversely affected by government proposals on child support reforms.
- The nuclear family is the central part of Finnish family life. Distant relatives are kept at bay, a study shows.
- Interior minister Jan-Erik Enestam says refugees from former Yugoslavia will not be sent home against their will.
- Former Russian ambassador to Hungary Ivan Aboimov to be posted to Helsinki early next year. Just turned 60, Aboimov has never visited Finland.

- "Better follow what Sweden does and not what she says," said Finnish Prime minister Paavo Lipponen who believes contrary to its pronouncements Sweden will be among the first to join the third phase of EMU.
- International rating institutions Standard & Poor's and Moody's to visit Finland and assess credit-worthiness soon.
- Revived Finnish Communist Party to be registered.
HUFVUDSTADSBLADET

- Secret EU Commission report says Finland more in favour of federalistic EU policies than Sweden and Denmark; Finland also more willing to accept supranational decision-making in foreign and security policy.
- Finnish investment in stocks on recently opened Tallinn Stock Exchange amounts to 700 million markka, a surprisingly big figure according to analysts. Hansapank most popular stock.
KAUPPALEHTI
- Employment in construction growing by 10 percent from last year.
- Building competitiveness on a weaker currency is not beneficial in the long term, says Bank of Finland economist Juhana Hukkinen.
DEMARI
- Former President Urho Kekkonen was no KGB agent, says researcher Hannu Rautkallio in a newly published book.
AAMULEHTI
- Business acquisitions to come under legal regulation in Finland, says Trade and Industry minister Antti Kalliomaki
- President Martti Ahtisaari not interested in meeting this year's Nobel peace laureate Jose Ramos-Horta, currently visiting Finland.
TURUN SANOMAT
- A 54-hour disco to be organised in Turku market square as part of a national youth festival.
